_refresh_policy.process: 1. Review OWASP LLM/Agentic Top 10 releases and known jailbreak-family reports. 2. Add probes with own-phrased signatures (never copy AGPL/copyrighted prompt text verbatim). 3. Bump version. 4. Run npm test (prober tests enforce compilation + ReDoS guard).

description: Prompt-injection probe corpus. Each entry is a static-detectable signal (regex) that a code path is constructing or accepting an LLM prompt in a way that matches a known injection class.

categories.title: Indirect injection from URL / file / RAG
Unsanitized user input into prompt construction
Obfuscated injection payloads (invisible chars, homoglyphs, cipher instructions)

probes.title: User input concatenated into system prompt
probes.description: User-controlled value is interpolated directly into a system prompt. This is the canonical direct prompt-injection pattern.
probes.fix: Keep system prompts static. If user data must influence behavior, treat it as untrusted user-role content and constrain it via templated placeholders or guardrails.

probes.title: Hardcoded instruction-override phrase
probes.description: Source contains a hardcoded instruction-override string. If this string is sent to a downstream LLM unsanitized, it is a self-jailbreak.
probes.fix: Remove hardcoded override phrases from prompts. If demonstrating the pattern in tests/docs, use the praxis-ignore inline comment.

probes.title: DAN / persona-bypass prompt
probes.description: Source contains a DAN-style or persona-bypass jailbreak template.
probes.fix: Strip jailbreak templates from prompts. Add prompt-injection detection on user input.

probes.title: Fetched URL content fed to LLM without sanitization
probes.description: Remote-fetched content flows into an LLM call without an intermediate sanitation step. This is the indirect-injection pattern (attacker plants instructions in a webpage / file).
probes.fix: Strip HTML, neutralize known jailbreak phrases, or render fetched content inside a delimited user-role block before sending to the LLM.

probes.title: RAG retrieved chunk concatenated into prompt
probes.description: RAG retrieval result is interpolated into a prompt without filtering. Attackers who can poison the retrieval index (e.g., via uploaded docs) gain prompt control.
probes.fix: Quote retrieved content inside delimited blocks (e.g., <document>...</document>) and instruct the model to treat them as untrusted data.

probes.title: System prompt echo via 'repeat your instructions' handling
probes.description: Code contains text that asks the model to disclose its system prompt — typical of prompt-extraction probing or a misconfigured debug path.
probes.fix: Never echo system prompts in production. Add a refusal pattern for prompt-disclosure requests.

probes.title: Over-broad tool / function schema (additionalProperties true / no validation)
probes.description: Tool/function schema is permissive: additionalProperties is true or there is no property constraint, so a model coerced via prompt injection can pass arbitrary args.
probes.fix: Define a strict JSON Schema for every tool: list required properties and set additionalProperties: false.

probes.title: Function-call result executed without confirmation
probes.description: Arguments coming from an LLM function call are passed straight into shell/exec/eval. A successful prompt injection becomes RCE.
probes.fix: Validate function-call arguments against a schema and require human confirmation for any side-effectful tool.

probes.title: User input wrapped in delimiters that the user can close
probes.description: User content is wrapped in delimiters (triple backticks, ChatML tokens) that the user can themselves emit, escaping the intended block.
probes.fix: Encode/escape special tokens in user input or use a delimiter unlikely to appear in user content.

probes.title: Anthropic Messages API: user role concatenated from raw input
probes.description: User role content is constructed by string interpolation from request data — sanitize first and consider rate-limiting / token caps.
probes.fix: Pass user input as a structured message rather than via template-string concatenation. Apply input length limits.

probes.title: Developer-mode jailbreak frame
probes.description: Source contains a developer-mode jailbreak frame that instructs a model to drop content restrictions. A classic jailbreak wrapper; near-zero legitimate use in application code.
probes.fix: Remove the jailbreak frame. Filter or refuse model inputs matching these frames at runtime.

probes.title: Uncensored-assistant persona
probes.description: Source contains an uncensored-assistant persona prompt with a never-refuse directive. Unambiguous jailbreak signal.
probes.fix: Remove the persona prompt. Never ship system prompts that promise not to refuse requests.

probes.title: Fictional / hypothetical framing
probes.description: Source contains a fictional/hypothetical jailbreak frame asking for a how-to. Common in legit security education too — review the surrounding context.
probes.fix: Review context. If this prompt string is shipped to a model, add output policy checks.

probes.title: AI-safety-researcher persona spoof
probes.description: Source spoofs an AI-safety-researcher persona to request analysis. A known jailbreak persona; medium confidence since red-team tooling also contains such phrasing.
probes.fix: Review context. Treat model-facing copies of this text as untrusted input.

probes.title: End-of-system-prompt delimiter token
probes.description: Source contains a system-prompt end delimiter. Legitimate in tokenizer/inference code (constants); adversarial when emitted inside user-controllable content.
probes.fix: If this string can reach user content, escape or strip it. Keep delimiter constants out of prompt templates.

probes.title: Fake system-rule header injection
probes.description: Source contains a fake markdown system-rule header used to smuggle override instructions past a model's real system prompt.
probes.fix: Strip fake system headers from untrusted content. Use delimiters users cannot guess.

probes.title: Decode-then-respond instruction
probes.description: Source contains a decode-then-respond instruction — an injection trope that makes a model execute hidden content before answering.
probes.fix: Never accept decode-first instructions from untrusted content. Sandbox any transformer step.

probes.title: Custom cipher / substitution-alphabet instruction
probes.description: Source contains a custom-cipher instruction (learn-my-alphabet) used to smuggle payloads past content filters.
probes.fix: Review context. Refuse ciphered instruction sets in untrusted model input.

probes.title: Zero-width / invisible characters (EchoLeak class)
probes.description: Source contains invisible Unicode characters (zero-width space/joiner, BOM, word joiner, Mongolian vowel separator). The canonical EchoLeak / CVE-2025-32711-class steganography vehicle. A leading U+FEFF may be a benign BOM — verify position.
probes.fix: Strip invisible characters from prompt-facing content. Hex-dump the line to inspect what is hidden.

probes.title: Bidi control characters
probes.description: Source contains bidi control characters (RLO/LRI/PDI/FSI). These reorder text visually to hide instructions or filenames from human review.
probes.fix: Strip bidi controls from untrusted content and display paths.

probes.title: Stacked combining marks (Zalgo text)
probes.description: Source contains runs of 3+ stacked combining diacritics — the Zalgo obfuscation signature used to hide payloads from filters and humans.
probes.fix: Normalize (NFC) and strip combining-mark runs from prompt-facing content.

probes.title: Unicode tag-block steganography
probes.description: Source contains characters from the Unicode Tags block (U+E0000–U+E00FF) — invisible characters used exclusively for steganographic payloads.
probes.fix: Strip all tag-block characters. They have no legitimate role in source code.

probes.title: Mixed-script homoglyph word
probes.description: Source contains a word mixing Latin and Cyrillic letters — the homoglyph technique (e.g. 'bypass' written with a Cyrillic 'у'). Legit mixed-language text exists; inspect the word.
probes.fix: Inspect the flagged word. Normalize confusable scripts (NFKC) in identifiers and prompt content.
